NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>SOURCE 1 shows the street elevation: a right brick volume with a narrow stacked window, left dark vertical cladding, two recessed balconies, a raised glazed rooftop volume, recessed ground-floor entrance, and brick frontage walls with gates. SOURCE 2–6 show the old model from opposite rear corners, above, and both front corners; shared rooftop and window landmarks establish orientation, but these problem-model screenshots do not independently verify the actual building’s hidden sides or roof construction. CURRENT preserves the principal front arrangement and opening positions. The clearest remaining discrepancies are the compressed ground storey and low frontage walls. No obvious floating balcony connection is visible; concealed joints and absolute dimensions remain unverified.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: Compared with SOURCE 1, CURRENT 13 compresses the ground storey beneath the continuous dark beam. The entrance and adjacent glazing are too squat relative to the closely matching upper facade.
action: Increase the ground-storey height locally, retaining the upper facade’s opening layout and balcony relationships. Match the beam-to-entry-threshold proportion to the photograph.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="front">problem: CURRENT’s frontage brick walls and gates are substantially shallower vertically than those in SOURCE 1, exposing too much ground-floor glazing and weakening the enclosed entrance composition.
action: Raise the front wall tops and adjoining gates to the photograph’s proportions relative to the entrance and beam; preserve their horizontal opening locations.</issue>
<keep>Three upper panes across the rooftop front glazing.
Right-hand narrow window stack with paired upper lights and single-width lower lights.
Two central balconies, with the lower balcony wider than the upper.
Brick notch above the lower balcony’s right-hand reveal.</keep>
